An Imperial Week in Photos: Princess Aiko Visits Ise Jingu

The Sankei Shimbun August 10, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:41
Instaread
Highlights include Princess Aiko's visit to Mie Prefecture and the Crown Prince and Princess' tour of Shiga for a national high school athletic meet.

Princess Aiko, the daughter of Emperor Naruhito and Empress Masako, pulls a rope during the Okihiki timber-hauling event in Ise, Mie Prefecture, on August 2.

このページを 日本語 で読む

Emperor Naruhito, Empress Masako and their daughter, Princess Aiko, conveyed their condolences through an aide on August 3 to Kumamoto Governor Takashi Kimura following the magnitude-7.1 earthquake that struck the region.

On August 6, the Imperial family offered silent prayers at the Imperial Palace to mark the anniversary of the atomic bombing of Hiroshima. Emperor Emeritus Akihito and Empress Emerita Michiko also watched a televised broadcast of the ceremony from their residence in Tokyo's Minato Ward and offered silent prayers.

On July 31, Empress Masako attended a ceremony at the Momijiyama Imperial Cocoonery on the grounds of the Imperial Palace marking the completion of this year's silkworm-rearing activities.

According to the Imperial Household Agency, she presented bundles of white and yellow raw silk produced from the harvested cocoons before an altar and paid her respects.

Visiting Mie Prefecture

Princess Aiko visited Mie Prefecture on August 1 and 2 to observe preparations for the Shikinen Sengu, a ritual held every 20 years in which the buildings of Ise Jingu are ceremonially reconstructed.

On August 1, she visited the Yamada Workshop in Ise, where construction work on the shrine buildings is carried out, and observed craftsmen marking timber with ink before cutting and shaping the wood.

She then visited Toba Aquarium, where she learned about the feeding of the dugong kept there.

The following day, Princess Aiko visited the Outer Shrine and Inner Shrine of Ise Jingu. She also observed the Kawabiki ("river pulling"), an event in which timber for the reconstruction of the shrine buildings is pulled upstream along the Isuzu River as part of the timber-hauling festival.

Princess Aiko, dressed in a white happi coat, helped pull the ropes attached to a wooden sled carrying timber.

She later visited the Jingu Chokokan Museum, where she viewed ceremonial garments, furnishings and other items that had been used in previous Shikinen Sengu ceremonies. She asked questions about the ceremonial attire and other exhibits.

High School Athletic Meet

Crown Prince Akishino (Fumihito) and Crown Princess Kiko visited Shiga Prefecture on August 2 and 3 to attend the opening ceremony of the National High School Athletic Meet. On the first day, they watched weightlifting competitions.

They later visited a workshop in Takashima where traditional fan ribs are made and observed craftsmen at work.

At the opening ceremony on August 3, the Crown Prince expressed his hope that "athletes and supporters from across the country, together with local high school students, will make the event a success, deepen their friendships and create fond memories of their high school years."

Other Engagements

Princess Akiko of Mikasa visited Yamagata Prefecture from August 2 to 4 to attend the 47th National Junior High School Shogi Championship.

Her younger sister, Princess Yoko, attended a ceremony marking the 50th anniversary of Japan's Water Day in Tokyo's Minato Ward on July 31.

Princess Takamado visited Okayama Prefecture from July 31 to August 1 to attend the 57th national women's recreational volleyball championship. She serves as honorary president of the organizing federation.

Princess Takamado, who also serves as honorary president of the Japan Handball Association, visited Ariake Arena in Tokyo on August 4 and 5 to watch matches in the Paris Saint-Germain Handball Japan Tour 2026.

Princess Tsuguko, Princess Takamado's eldest daughter, visited Osaka Prefecture on August 5 to watch archery competitions at the National High School Athletic Meet and for other engagements. Princess Tsuguko serves as honorary president of the All Japan Archery Federation.
